nodes.label: Event and Delivery Path
nodes.rationale: The relay publishes only the event ID and the consumer reloads the durable envelope, so the message carries an identifier rather than business data and Redis never becomes an authority.

nodes.label: Gated Rebuild Path
nodes.rationale: Resumable staging-table rebuild is deferred until measured volume makes the simpler gated replay operationally unacceptable.

nodes.label: Payments Tracer Bullet
nodes.rationale: Normal path and rebuild path reuse the same deterministic projection application service, and rebuild never republishes integration side effects.

nodes.label: Shared DatabaseTransactionsManager Callback Locality
nodes.rationale: Every connection is handed the same singleton manager and addCallback() attaches to getPendingTransactions()->last() across all connections, so callback locality is accidental and must be asserted rather than assumed. A commit fires callbacks; a rollback discards them.

nodes.label: Lock-Through-Push Relay Algorithm
nodes.rationale: One row per transaction with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, publishing immediately inside the transaction rather than through an after-commit callback; short transport timeouts, a bounded batch and a maximum wall-clock runtime prevent unbounded database occupancy. Overlapping relay invocations are safe because row locks, not scheduler uniqueness, provide correctness.

nodes.label: Outbox Delivery State Transitions
nodes.rationale: Accepted publication does not consume poison budget; rejected publication records transport failure and bounded exponential backoff while leaving last_published_at unchanged, so an arbitrarily long transport outage never sets exhausted_at. Only a confirmed consumer-handler exception increments the poison count; worker termination, backlog and a missing receipt are not poison evidence.

nodes.label: Idempotent Consumer Transaction
nodes.rationale: A durable projector receipt keyed by (projector_name, event_id) is the idempotency boundary. A duplicate leaves PaymentDetails unchanged and fills only a missing completion marker; a receipt whose read row is missing is corruption for verification/rebuild, not an excuse to silently recreate state. A payment_id collision from another source event is contradictory history and must fail visibly rather than be hidden by an upsert.

nodes.label: Deterministic Projection Derivation
nodes.rationale: initiated_at derives from event occurred_at, never processing time, randomness or live mutable data; aggregate version is retained so later lifecycle events can detect out-of-order delivery, and the first-event slice builds no generic deferral framework.

nodes.label: Projection Failure Handling
nodes.rationale: Confirmed handler failure metadata is recorded separately from the rolled-back projection transaction; work deferred by the rebuild gate consumes neither transport nor poison budgets, and stale messages after a successful rebuild are ignored by recreated projector receipts.

nodes.label: Payments Projection Gate
nodes.rationale: payment_projection_controls is durable operator-visible state while advisory locks own mutual exclusion. Readers take a transaction-scoped shared lock on the same explicit connection; rebuild holds a session-level exclusive lock on one pinned connection. Losing or reconnecting the pinned session aborts the rebuild — code never assumes the old lock survived.

nodes.label: Gated Rebuild Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Lock timeout aborts before clearing data; a handled error or process death leaves the durable row as rebuilding even though PostgreSQL releases the session lock, and the next authorized run clears partial derived state and restarts from zero. Guarded recovery may set ready without replay only if it proves no clear or partial replay began.

nodes.label: timestampTz(6) Precision Requirement
nodes.rationale: Schema\Builder::$defaultTimePrecision is 0, so a bare $table->timestamp() yields timestamp(0) in PostgreSQL and rounds to whole seconds; every Payments-owned timestamp therefore declares timestampTz(…, 6).

nodes.label: Evolution Gate: Claim/Lease Publishing
nodes.rationale: Lock-through-push is intentionally simple; a claim/lease redesign is triggered only by sustained measurement — pool saturation or >20% API p95 regression, oldest eligible age over five seconds for five continuous minutes with a healthy transport, or unmeetable throughput after tuning. A transient transport outage alone is not a trigger.

nodes.label: Deferred Resumable Staging-Table Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Required only when measured event volume, rebuild duration or restart cost violates an availability target; that future design must cover staging lifecycle, events arriving during replay, final catch-up, atomic swap, cleanup, and crash recovery at every transition.

nodes.label: AggregateRoot Four-Call Lifecycle
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: retrieve() resolves a new instance through the container so every call yields a distinct object, which makes a fresh aggregate per retry attempt achievable without extra machinery; loadUuid() reuses the instance and does not.

nodes.label: Projector Auto-Discovery Scans app/ Only
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: auto_discover_projectors_and_reactors defaults to [app()->path()] and never scans Modules/, so module handlers must be registered explicitly through Projectionist::addProjector().

nodes.label: Laravel ConcurrencyErrorDetector Cannot Express the Retry Allowlist
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.norm_label: laravel concurrencyerrordetector cannot express the retry allowlist
nodes.rationale: It matches 40001 by code, detects 40P01 only through the English message 'deadlock detected', and does not recognize 55P03 at all — measured returning false against a real PostgreSQL 18.4 lock conflict. The repository must own its own SQLSTATE matching.

nodes.label: Duplicate Aggregate Version Never Reaches SQLSTATE Classification
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.norm_label: duplicate aggregate version never reaches sqlstate classification
nodes.rationale: persistWithoutApplyingToEventHandlers() catches UniqueConstraintViolationException from the (aggregate_uuid, aggregate_version) constraint and rethrows CouldNotPersistAggregate::invalidVersion(), so any retry policy keyed on SQLSTATE will not see it.

nodes.label: Observed SQLSTATE Exception Shape
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Both 55P03 and 23505 wrap a PDOException and carry the SQLSTATE in errorInfo[0] and getCode() as a string, so comparison against an integer silently never matches.

nodes.label: persist() Opens No Transaction
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: AggregateRoot::persist() calls persistWithoutApplyingToEventHandlers() and handles stored events inline; only persistInTransaction() wraps work in DB::transaction(). The caller's transaction is therefore the only one, which is what the Payments atomic write needs. persist() writes each event twice (INSERT then UPDATE of meta_data), which does not disturb xmin.

nodes.label: Nested Transaction Needed After an Expected Constraint Violation
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.norm_label: nested transaction needed after an expected constraint violation
nodes.rationale: A failed statement aborts the whole transaction, so a test expecting a violation and then continuing must wrap the failing statement in a nested transaction (SAVEPOINT / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT) or every later statement returns 25P02.

nodes.label: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.norm_label: spatie event sourcing as actually installed
nodes.rationale: Read from vendor source at 7.15.1 rather than from documentation: it publishes migrations without loading them, merges config without publishing, and its behavior is cited by file and line.

nodes.label: Handlers Run Inline Unless ShouldQueue
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: StoredEvent::handle() calls handleWithSyncEventHandlers() first and only dispatches a job for handlers that are ShouldQueue; the event-sourcing.queue config names the queue but does not decide whether one is used.

nodes.label: ADR 0003 PostgreSQL Idempotency Arbitration
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed

nodes.label: Atomic Write Sequence
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Immutable command context — canonical input, candidate payment UUID, event UUID, occurrence time and the once-serialized success body — is built before the transaction opens, so identifiers and response bytes cannot drift between attempts.

nodes.label: T6 Implementation Evidence (C1-C7)
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: The commit-boundary suite runs without RefreshDatabase deliberately: the trait turns the production DB::transaction() into a savepoint so TransactionCommitting never fires at depth 1 and an 'all three rows exist' assertion would pass against a handler that opened no transaction at all. The suite refuses to run if it finds itself wrapped and provisions its own schema.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE Retry Allowlist
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Only 40P01, 40001 and 55P03 retry the whole outer closure, at most three attempts, with fresh aggregate and event objects but stable IDs, occurrence time, fingerprint and response bytes. Laravel's inner transaction uses one attempt so retry budgets do not multiply; exhaustion returns 503 with Retry-After: 1 and no partial state.

nodes.label: PaymentOutboxWriter Synchronous Projector
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Registered explicitly by PaymentsServiceProvider because auto_discover_projectors_and_reactors only looks in app/. It reads the payload back out of stored_events.event_properties by primary key on the same connection inside the same transaction, so jsonb-equality is true by construction rather than by test, and it refuses loudly when isReplaying() is true because a replayed event is fully derivable and a rebuild would otherwise re-create envelopes or die on the aggregate-version unique reporting the wrong problem.

nodes.label: catch_exceptions Pinned to Literal false
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Projectionist copies the flag when the singleton is built, so changing config later has no effect; a true value would silently break outbox atomicity by committing a stored event without its outbox row. T5 pinned a literal false so no environment variable can set it, proved by a test that requires the file and scans for env() tokens because the merged runtime value is false either way.

nodes.label: snapshots Table Required Though Never Written
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.norm_label: snapshots table required though never written
nodes.rationale: reconstituteFromEvents() calls getSnapshotRepository()->retrieve() unconditionally on both uuid-binding paths and no configuration switch skips it; the alternative buys one empty table at the price of an aggregate that cannot be replayed.

nodes.label: SQLSTATE Extraction and DeadlockException Unwrapping
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Read errorInfo[0] with getCode() as fallback and unwrap DeadlockException first: it extends PDOException but carries no errorInfo of its own, so an unwrapped read returns null and misclassifies a retryable failure as fatal. Both carry the SQLSTATE as a string, so comparison against an integer silently never matches.

nodes.label: Named ON CONFLICT Target
nodes.community_name: Spatie Event Sourcing As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: The conflict target is named, not omitted, because the receipts table also carries a global unique on payment_id and an untargeted clause would swallow that collision too, turning a permanent condition into a retryable 503. Recorded in ADR 0003 and proved by a pre-seeded receipt colliding on payment_id surfacing as internal_error rather than idempotency_contention.

nodes.label: payments-projection Redis Queue
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL remains the authority; Redis failure can delay projection delivery but cannot erase the payment event or the durable outbox intent. At-least-once delivery and duplicate handling are part of the application contract.

nodes.label: Application Process Topology
nodes.rationale: Processes reuse the ledgerflow-api image where practical but remain independently supervised, scaled, restarted and observed. The first Payments slice requires only HTTP/API, Horizon and scheduler/relay.

nodes.label: Scheduler/Relay Process
nodes.rationale: Heartbeat and oldest eligible outbox age must expose a stopped scheduler even when HTTP and workers are healthy.

nodes.label: Docker Container Contract
nodes.rationale: A custom production-oriented Dockerfile rather than Sail; the entrypoint ends in exec "$@" with CMD ["php-fpm"], so Horizon, scheduler/relay, Reverb and future SQS workers reuse the same image with only a command override.

nodes.label: Redis/Horizon Queue Transport Policy
nodes.rationale: M1-M5 use Redis so relay, duplicates, Horizon supervision, failed jobs and local recovery are easy to observe; the projection job and envelope must not depend on Redis types, and PostgreSQL outbox state plus projector receipts remain authoritative for recovery.

nodes.label: payments:outbox:relay Scheduler Contract
nodes.rationale: A short-lived command scheduled every second; production must supervise a scheduler process and interrupt the previous release after new code is live, and heartbeat plus oldest eligible age must expose a stopped scheduler even when HTTP and workers are healthy.

nodes.label: OpenSearch Adoption Gate
nodes.rationale: OpenSearch is not provisioned for portfolio completeness; adoption requires a query PostgreSQL cannot serve, specified indexing/replay/consistency ownership, a justified cost, and understood security/backup/deletion requirements. Until then PostgreSQL projections are the default search source.

nodes.label: One Image, Independently Supervised Processes
nodes.rationale: The API image may run HTTP/Filament, Horizon, scheduler/relay, Reverb and future SQS workers; reusing an image does not merge their scaling, health, or restart ownership.

nodes.label: SQS Adoption Boundary
nodes.rationale: SQS/DLQ is added only for a distinct workload benefiting from AWS-native durable delivery, visibility timeouts, redrive and independently scalable workers; the first concrete workload must be selected and specified before implementation. Horizon does not supervise SQS.

nodes.label: One Job, One Transport Rule
nodes.rationale: Never dual-publish one logical job to Redis and SQS merely to exercise both technologies; a legitimate fan-out requires two explicit integration messages with their own owners, idempotency contracts and failure policies.

nodes.label: AWS Readiness Gates
nodes.rationale: Before deployment a process must define command/config/health/shutdown contracts, validation and smoke evidence, ECS ownership and scaling, IAM and secret boundaries, logs/metrics/alarms/runbooks, and rollback compatibility for database or message changes.

nodes.label: ADR 0002 Payments Domain Event-Sourcing Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Payments Domain may reference exactly two external Spatie classes matched as exact names in that module only; Projector is named and excluded because it writes a read model and belongs in Infrastructure. Widening the allowlist would grant Domain a type it must never reference.

nodes.label: PaymentInitiated Event Contract
nodes.rationale: A final class extending ShouldBeStored with six public readonly promoted properties that are exactly the durable payload keys; constructor validation is the last line of defence, not the user-facing one, since request validation returns 422 first.

nodes.label: Enforced Architecture Rules
nodes.rationale: Payments Domain cannot depend on Laravel, Eloquent, HTTP, Redis, SQS or queue types; only ADR-listed Spatie base types are allowed; raw concurrency SQL stays inside its focused Payments Infrastructure owner; queries never rehydrate PaymentAggregate.

nodes.label: Event Class Map Alias
nodes.rationale: The package requires no class map, but the alias is what lets the namespace move without rewriting history. enforce_event_class_map stays false because T3/T4 spikes persist test-only fixtures that must never enter production configuration; an exact-equality test on the map enforces completeness instead. The dotted key is safe because Arr::get() checks Arr::exists() before splitting on '.'.

nodes.label: eventVersion() Override Instead of #[EventVersion]
nodes.rationale: The attribute would be a third vendor type in Domain, which ADR 0002 forbids; Spatie's ObjectNormalizer filters eventVersion out of the payload unless the child declares a property of that name, so the override changes the stored key set not at all — measured, not assumed.

nodes.label: occurredAt Stored as a String
nodes.rationale: Symfony's DateTimeNormalizer sits in Spatie's default chain and formats with RFC3339, which has no sub-second component, so a DateTimeImmutable property would silently truncate business time to whole seconds inside the stored payload.

nodes.label: Alias Is Stable Identity, Not Class Name
nodes.norm_label: alias is stable identity, not class name
nodes.rationale: PaymentInitiated::ALIAS is payments.payment_initiated and is what stored_events.event_class and payment_outbox.event_type carry, so the namespace can move without rewriting history.

nodes.label: MerchantContext Tenant Resolution
nodes.rationale: A merchant identifier supplied by a client is never sufficient authority; ownership is resolved server-side from the authenticated user.

nodes.label: Sanctum As Actually Installed
nodes.rationale: Sanctum 4.3.3 calls publishesMigrations() and never loadMigrationsFrom(), so personal_access_tokens does not exist until published; config/sanctum.php also needed a (string) cast on env() to pass Larastan level 10. No guard entry was added to config/auth.php because an unnecessary one is configuration nobody can later tell is load-bearing.

nodes.label: POST /api/payments HTTP Contract
nodes.rationale: The idempotency key is merchant-scoped so two merchants may use the same value independently; ownership comes from the authenticated user and client-selected ownership is rejected.

nodes.label: Frontend Deployment Gate
nodes.rationale: SSR/runtime hosting on ECR+Fargate versus a static S3/CloudFront build must be chosen from authentication, realtime, caching and product needs before implementation; the choice belongs to the SPA and infra repos, not backend code.

nodes.label: Deferred Sanctum/SPA Session Decisions
nodes.rationale: T6 deliberately decided nothing above the token: abilities unscoped, expiration null, cookie-versus-token mode, CORS, CSRF and deployment domains open. A server-to-server bearer test is evidence the guard works, not a selection of the SPA session mode; these move to Merchant dashboard integration.

nodes.label: Queue Failure Ownership
nodes.rationale: No queue is disposable merely because work can be replayed; every logical queue must define lag, failure, retry, poison and recovery evidence. Filament and the merchant dashboard expose no raw queue or DLQ controls.

nodes.label: Required Operational Evidence
nodes.rationale: Structured logs exclude raw idempotency keys and include payment, merchant, event, message and correlation identifiers. The verifier reports corruption; it never repairs or rebuilds automatically.

nodes.label: Raw Idempotency Key Never Persisted or Logged
nodes.norm_label: raw idempotency key never persisted or logged
nodes.rationale: Hashing gives fixed-width lookup and reduces casual plaintext exposure; it is not encryption. T6's test drives 202, 409 and 422 through one key then scans every column of every row of three tables as encoded JSON plus every captured log line, so a future column carrying the key fails it, and the listener is asserted non-empty so the log half cannot pass vacuously.

nodes.label: payments:projections:verify Read-Only Verification
nodes.rationale: The application cannot infer corruption from elapsed time — a missing projection may still be valid queue lag — so verification classifies events newer than delivery grace as in-flight, never mutates data, and never starts a rebuild automatically.

nodes.label: payments:outbox:repair Targeted Repair
nodes.rationale: Explicit and audited: it reconstructs only the derived envelope from the canonical stored event, refuses an orphan envelope without one, and never creates or changes an idempotency receipt. Bulk repair is separate reviewed scope.

nodes.label: Filament Admin Boundary
nodes.rationale: Filament serves business workflows only; it must not generically mutate stored events, projections, outbox rows, payment status, queue state or AWS resources. A business action calls the same Application command and domain invariants as an API action.

nodes.label: Known Deferred Concerns
nodes.rationale: public/storage is not served, Pest suites are not statically analysed (the trailing /* in the PHPStan exclusion is load-bearing), .env edits need make start, make test leaves postgres and redis running, the database half of the env fix has no test, and CI has no Docker layer caching because buildx would not be shared locally.

nodes.label: Test-Only Spike Artifacts and Blast Radius
nodes.norm_label: test-only spike artifacts and blast radius
nodes.rationale: The spike writes Redis logical database 15 with an empty prefix and deletes only the eight keys it can create by name — never KEYS *, flushdb or flushall; database 15 reduces blast radius but is not claimed as exclusively owned, correctness comes from the key list. The harness is not parallel-safe, so make test deliberately does not pass --parallel.

nodes.label: Spike Harness Limits
nodes.rationale: Three connections against one ledgerflow_test database — a RefreshDatabase-wrapped observer, an unwrapped unit under test, and an unwrapped lock supplier — because work on the wrapped default connection would be a savepoint that never commits. Not parallel-safe; retry is proved single-process.

nodes.label: T3 Blocking Compatibility Evidence (Q1-Q5)
nodes.rationale: Proved atomic three-row persistence on one backend by shared xmin and one pg_backend_pid, rollback at two failure boundaries, a synchronous handler that enqueues nothing, a real 55P03 retried with fresh objects, exhaustion at three attempts, and a real 23505 attempted once. 40P01 and 40001 were not produced and are not claimed.

nodes.label: $_SERVER Environment-Precedence Defect and Repair
nodes.rationale: PHPUnit <env force="true"> writes putenv() and $_ENV but never $_SERVER, which Laravel's resolver reads first, so QUEUE_CONNECTION, CACHE_STORE and SESSION_DRIVER silently lost to Compose's env_file and the suite's default queue was a real Redis queue on logical database 0. tests/bootstrap.php now validates and forces all three into all three sources, and InfrastructureContractTest asserts the live SyncQueue, ArrayStore and array session driver.

nodes.label: Test Environment Rules
nodes.rationale: SQLite is not a substitute for PostgreSQL concurrency and advisory-lock behavior; queue/database fakes are used only when the faked boundary is not the behavior under test, and a future SQS workload gets its own transport and DLQ plan rather than implicitly replacing the Redis projection suite.

nodes.label: Failure Injection Discipline
nodes.rationale: Process tests use synchronization barriers then SIGTERM/SIGKILL real relay, consumer and rebuild processes; arbitrary sleeps are not accepted as coordination, and production logic contains no environment-conditioned fault flags.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions OIDC Role Assumption
nodes.rationale: Bounded AWS roles assumed via OIDC so no long-lived AWS keys are committed or stored as ordinary repository secrets.

nodes.label: User Interface Surface Ownership
nodes.rationale: ledgerflow-spa never reads the database, Redis, queues, or AWS services directly; it consumes stable API contracts and authorized realtime events.

nodes.label: Reverb WebSocket Boundary
nodes.rationale: Redis Pub/Sub is transient fan-out, not a durable queue, and cannot be the authority for a payment transition; the browser recovers missed state through an API read after reconnecting.

nodes.label: Redis/SQS Capability Map
nodes.rationale: Similar infrastructure names must not collapse distinct delivery semantics: Redis cache, locks, Pub/Sub, Redis queues and SQS are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: Source-of-Truth Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: stored_events and idempotency receipts are not rebuildable; outbox, projector receipts and payment_details are derived. A Redis or SQS message is a transient delivery attempt never treated as truth.

nodes.label: Three-Repository Ownership Split
nodes.rationale: Application repos build immutable artifacts tagged by commit SHA; ledgerflow-infra consumes them rather than cloning and building application source, so infrastructure deployment never rebuilds application code.

nodes.label: Payments-Specific Transactional Outbox Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over direct event-store catch-up because it makes the database-to-broker failure window observable and recoverable, demonstrates relay crash recovery and idempotent consumption, and keeps the durable envelope independent of Redis. Trade-offs: more schema, retry state, tooling and tests; the relay holds a row lock through a bounded network push; deliberately Payments-specific with no shared bus justified by one use case.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Owns Durable Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Rate limiting can reduce request frequency but cannot prove retries create one business operation; a Redis lock may later reduce contention but is never authoritative. Reservation, PaymentInitiated, outbox creation and the exact successful response commit atomically on one connection.

nodes.label: Durable Outbox With ID-Only Publication
nodes.rationale: A transport outage is not the same failure as a deterministic poison message; treating publication as completion can lose projections while retrying blindly creates duplicates or exhausts healthy work. The relay publishes an event ID and the consumer loads the canonical envelope from PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: GET /api/payments/{paymentId}
nodes.rationale: Queries never rehydrate the aggregate; they read only PaymentDetails and the merchant-owned idempotency receipt.

nodes.label: RFC 9457 Problem Details Surface
nodes.rationale: T6 defines seven codes so no /api/* failure can escape in another shape; type is the relative URI reference /problems/{code} and code is the stable identifier everything else derives from. projection_rebuilding and payment_not_found belong to T9 and deliberately do not exist yet, because an enum case with no producer is a promise nothing keeps.

nodes.label: Eventual-Consistency Query Contract
nodes.rationale: Another merchant's payment returns the same not-found shape; the endpoint never rehydrates PaymentAggregate and never treats Redis/SQS state as proof that a payment exists.

nodes.label: No Dependency Without a Consumer
nodes.rationale: laravel/pail was removed and spatie/laravel-data deferred because a package with no consumer is a dependency with no consumer; laravel-data arrives only with the first DTO needing casting, transformation, or more than one representation.

nodes.label: Exception-Type-First Problem Mapping
nodes.rationale: Required rather than stylistic: Laravel's prepareJsonResponse() gives any non-HttpException a 500 before the hook runs, and Application-layer exceptions cannot implement Symfony's HttpExceptionInterface without breaking the module boundary rule, so a status-driven mapper would ship the 409 as a 500. detail is a fixed client-safe sentence because exception messages routinely carry SQL, table names and identifiers.

nodes.label: No CHECK Constraints on Counters Yet
nodes.norm_label: no check constraints on counters yet
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL has no unsigned integer so a check would be the only enforcement, but T5 ships none because no production writer exists — a constraint added now would guard columns nothing writes. T7 owns the invariant for publish_count and consecutive_transport_failures; T8 owns it for projection_failure_count.

nodes.label: Connection Loss and Stale transactionLevel()
nodes.rationale: Connection::run() rethrows only when transactions >= 1 and otherwise reconnects silently; reconnect() and disconnect() never touch the transaction counter, so transactionLevel() can outlive the backend it describes. Classification is substring matching on the message, not SQLSTATE — a terminated backend inside a transaction reports HY000, not 57P01.

nodes.label: Queue and Redis Configuration Caching
nodes.rationale: RedisManager captures database.redis when the singleton is built and QueueManager caches the resolved queue per name, so two behaviours need two configured names and a runtime-registered connection is visible only if the redis instance is forgotten first.

nodes.label: Laravel Queue Publication Path
nodes.rationale: push() routes through Queue::enqueueUsing() and consults shouldDispatchAfterCommit(); pushRaw() bypasses that check entirely and is unconditionally immediate. A job implementing ShouldQueueAfterCommit or carrying a truthy $afterCommit overrides the connection config. One push() writes exactly queues:<name> and queues:<name>:notify.

nodes.label: T4 Blocking Compatibility Evidence (Q6-Q10)
nodes.rationale: Advisory-lock affinity witnessed from a third connection through pg_locks, shared and exclusive contention with no sleeps including a real 55P03 from a bounded lock_timeout, silent reconnect versus surfaced loss with a stale transactionLevel(), Redis publication readable while the PostgreSQL transaction was still open, a non-vacuous after_commit control, and a crash after publication returning the row to eligible so a later pass produced the documented safe duplicate.

nodes.label: Constraints T7 Inherits
nodes.rationale: Publish with push(), never pushRaw(), because pushRaw skips enqueueUsing entirely and cannot express the after-commit question. The relay job must implement neither ShouldQueueAfterCommit nor a truthy $afterCommit, since those are checked before the connection config. A resolved queue connection caches its configuration, so two behaviours need two configured names. Measured queue keys are literally queues:<name> and queues:<name>:notify.

nodes.label: Neither a Successful Query Nor transactionLevel() Proves Lock Survival
nodes.norm_label: neither a successful query nor transactionlevel() proves lock survival
nodes.rationale: Outside a transaction Laravel reconnects silently onto a new backend with the advisory lock gone; inside one the loss surfaces but transactionLevel() still reports 1. Both can be true while the lock is already held by somebody else, so a rebuild inferring ownership from either is unsafe and the abort path needs a positive check — a re-read of the durable control row on a known-live connection, a fenced token, or a refusal to reconnect at all. T11 owns that choice; T4 only proves the naive inference is wrong.

nodes.label: PHPStan Level 10 With No Baseline
nodes.community_name: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.rationale: phpstan.neon forbids a baseline in writing; T5 populated the Payments Domain and level 10 still held, so the earlier prediction that the Payments slice would force a lowering did not come true. A future lowering must be explicit and reasoned.

nodes.label: What T5 Added
nodes.community_name: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.rationale: First production Payments code with no new dependency: Domain types, ADR 0002 and the narrowed allowlist, four migrations, a three-key config/event-sourcing.php, and module unit-test collection. Deliberately no commit-boundary evidence, concurrency, outbox writer, receipt writer, relay, query plan or snapshot write.

nodes.label: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.community_name: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.norm_label: payment_outbox envelope and partial active index
nodes.rationale: The hot-path partial index is (available_at, event_id) where projection_completed_at IS NULL AND exhausted_at IS NULL; a named unique (aggregate_uuid, aggregate_version) mirrors the stored_events key so a duplicate envelope is impossible rather than merely detectable, and can never fire spuriously because the source table cannot produce a colliding pair.

nodes.label: Five-Failure Exhaustion Threshold
nodes.community_name: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.rationale: Initial timings are operational defaults, not domain rules — a 30-second reconciliation grace, capped exponential backoff, and one application-level consumer attempt per published job — tunable by the load milestone without weakening acceptance tests. payments:outbox:retry {eventId} is the only path that clears exhausted_at.

nodes.label: 63-Byte Identifier Limit and Explicit Key Names
nodes.community_name: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.norm_label: 63-byte identifier limit and explicit key names
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL truncates identifiers at 63 bytes and a truncated name cannot be dropped by the name a later migration computes, so Payments-authored keys are named explicitly; the longest generated identifier measured is 58 characters.

nodes.label: Three-Task Outbox Writer Ownership Split
nodes.community_name: payment_outbox Envelope and Partial Active Index
nodes.rationale: T6 inserts the envelope, T7 mutates transport state only and never writes exhausted_at, T8 records consumer outcome and owns exhaustion. Exhaustion sits with T8 because only a confirmed consumer-handler exception increments the count that triggers it; splitting increment from threshold check across two owners would make the decision race on a stale value.

nodes.label: CI Contract Assertions
nodes.rationale: Guard, isolation, image-contract and failure-diagnostic assertions are contract assertions about the Makefile and image, not a second validation path that bypasses it.

nodes.label: Makefile Public Interface
nodes.rationale: All application validation runs through public Make targets; CI installs with make install and validates with the single make check contract and contains no Composer, Pest, Pint, Rector, PHPStan or Artisan invocation of its own.

nodes.label: Seeder Determinism Contract
nodes.rationale: A re-run creates no duplicate identities, never moves an email to a different merchant and never rewrites a password hash, but does not promise byte-identical rows; identities are keyed by slug and email because ids come from a sequence and are not stable across a rebuild, and the whole fixture set is written in one transaction.

nodes.label: What T3 Deliberately Did Not Add
nodes.community_name: What T3 Deliberately Did Not Add
nodes.norm_label: what t3 deliberately did not add
nodes.rationale: T3 is a compatibility spike: no production Payments types, no production schema, no published configuration, no Domain allowlist or ADR — because no vendor type entered production module code there was nothing to permit. Recorded so a reader does not go looking for artifacts that were never created.

nodes.label: What T4 Deliberately Did Not Add
nodes.community_name: What T3 Deliberately Did Not Add
nodes.norm_label: what t4 deliberately did not add
nodes.rationale: T4 added no dependency, no production types, no production schema, no configuration or phpunit.xml change, no Horizon/scheduler/relay/worker and no ADR; it registered its Redis and queue connections at runtime in a test-only harness.

nodes.label: First Vertical Slice Scenario
nodes.rationale: A convincing DDD/CQRS/ES showcase must demonstrate more than folders: a reviewer should be able to repeat a request, stop workers, redeliver work, corrupt derived state and rebuild it without creating contradictory business history.
